lesson: Translating physical situations into mathematical models
title: A skydiver approaches terminal velocity
caption: Setting weight equal to drag, mg = ½ρC_dAv², gives v_t = √(2mg/ρC_dA) = √1869 ≈ 43 m s⁻¹. The speed starts with slope g and flattens towards v_t; after about 10 s it is within 2% of it.
alt: Speed against time for a skydiver, rising from zero with slope g and levelling off at a dashed line at 43 metres per second.
description: With drag, v(t) = v_t tanh(gt/v_t); at t = 10 s v = 42.3 m s⁻¹.
At first drag is negligible and v ≈ gt.
